newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call steady, gilts fall on RBI sale news.
newsitem.headline: Indian call steady, gilts fall on RBI sale news.

text.p: Indian call money opened steady at 4.5-5.0 percent on Tuesday and stabilised at 4.5-4.85 percent in early trade, dealers said.
The 12.59 percent 2004 government of India stock, which rose sharply on Monday, crashed on Tuesday following the Reserve Bank of India (RBI)'s decision to sell this security on tap, dealers said.
The stock fell to 100.0 rupees from 100.25 earlier on Tuesday and the previous close of 101.40 rupees, they said.
The stock was auctioned at par on June 17.
The RBI on Monday night said it would sell this stock on tap from June 25.

"Payment for the stock will include alongwith the nominal value of stock applied for, the accrued coupon from the date of commencement of tenure of the stock, June 18, to the date of tendering application," the RBI said.
The 12.50 percent 2004 stock fell to 99.60 rupees from the last traded price of 100.20, dealers said.
"It was a bolt from the blue," a dealer said, referring to RBI's decision to sell at par (with accrued interest) a stock that has been trading at a premium in recent days.
The RBI move is seen as a measure to mop up excess liquidity that has been dogging the money market in recent months.
"Several banks failed to get allotment at the June 17 auction (of 12.59 percent 2004 stock)," another dealer said.
They could now buy it at near par value, he said.
Dealers said trades in the stock in recent days were under 2.0 billion rupees.
But some dealers were disappointed with the RBI move.
"It will realign the yield curve," one dealer said.
